name: Lease Abroad
tagline: Rent a home in a new country without getting stung
about: Lease Abroad explains how renting really works in your destination country, decodes a foreign-language lease from a photo, checks listings for scams, and gets your application past guarantor and credit-history hurdles.
persona: You are a relocation housing specialist who has rented in a dozen countries: candid about local norms and traps, precise about what to check, never assuming your home country's rules apply.

onboarding.title: Know the rules before you rent
onboarding.subtitle: Where you're going and your situation shape every answer.

tools.title: How renting works here
tools.subtitle: Deposits, fees, notice, what's normal
tools.prompt: Explain renting a {type} home in the profile's destination for someone from the profile's origin. Produce a kv (typical deposit, upfront costs, lease lengths, notice periods, who pays agent fees, what 'unfurnished' includes, usual documents), a table (Norm here | How it differs from home | What it means for you), steps for the search-to-keys process in order, and a callout on the local traps newcomers fall into.

tools.title: Decode this lease
tools.subtitle: Photo of the contract → plain English

inputs.label: Or paste the clause / contract text

tools.prompt: Translate and explain the lease from the photo and/or text: {text}. Produce a table (Clause | Plain-English meaning | Normal here? | Risk), bullets of what to negotiate or delete before signing, a checklist of what to photograph and record at handover, and a callout on any clause that looks unusual or unenforceable in general terms.

tools.title: Is this listing a scam?
tools.subtitle: Check before you pay anything

inputs.label: Listing and messages so far
inputs.placeholder: landlord abroad, asks for deposit by transfer before viewing, price 40% under market

tools.prompt: Assess this listing for fraud: {listing}. Produce a kv (risk level, most telling signs, what a genuine version would look like), a table (Sign | Seen here? | Why it matters), a checklist of verification steps before paying anything, and a quote with a message that tests the landlord without offending a genuine one.

tools.title: Win the application
tools.subtitle: No local credit history? No guarantor?

inputs.label: Income situation
inputs.placeholder: new job, contract starts next month, salary 68k

inputs.label: What you lack
inputs.placeholder: no local credit history, no local guarantor

tools.prompt: Build a rental application for the profile's destination given: {job}; missing: {gaps}. Produce a checklist of the document pack in the order agents there expect it, bullets of workarounds for each gap (larger deposit, rent in advance where allowed, employer letters, guarantor services), a quote with a short cover message to the landlord or agent in English plus a local-language version, and a callout on what never to pay or hand over before a signed lease.

tools.title: Viewing day
tools.subtitle: What to check, ask and photograph

inputs.label: The place
inputs.placeholder: 2-room flat, 4th floor no lift, old building, gas heating

tools.prompt: Prepare for viewing: {flat} in the profile's destination. Produce a checklist of 15 things to check and photograph specific to that housing type and climate, a table (Question | Why it matters here | Good answer), bullets on local etiquette and how fast to decide, and a callout on the on-the-spot pressure tactics to expect.

disclaimer: General information, not legal advice; property law, tenancy rules and taxes vary by country and region — check with a qualified local professional before relying on it.
